# 'I cannot say it'll all be the same': Satya Nadella on Microsoft's voluntary exit offer

**URL:** https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-makers/i-cannot-say-itll-all-be-the-same-satya-nadella-on-microsofts-voluntary-exit-offer-114933.htm
**Description:** Satya Nadella said Microsoft wants to help employees build skills for emerging roles, including opportunities in Windows and AI training, while giving them greater control over their long-term career decisions.
**Scraped:** 2026-11-17T14:54:52.116127+00:00

---

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has said the company's Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) is intended to give employees greater freedom to decide their career paths amid changes in job roles, organisational structures and the skills required across the technology industry.

In an interview on The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella said Microsoft expects the nature of opportunities within the company to evolve, making it necessary to rethink how teams operate and how employees are deployed across different functions.

He said the company wants to create fresh avenues for employees within the organisation while helping them develop capabilities that could benefit their careers beyond Microsoft as well.

Discussing the changing employment landscape, Nadella said there would continue to be opportunities at Microsoft, although the roles and responsibilities associated with them could look different in the future.

He pointed to areas such as Windows and AI training as examples of work where employees could develop skills relevant to emerging requirements. The company, he added, wants to ensure that its workforce is equipped to move into these areas.

Nadella also indicated that Microsoft's existing workforce would need to be organised differently as the company adapts to these changes. Referring to its workforce of around 200,000 employees, he said the organisation would have to reconsider team sizes and working arrangements.

Explaining the reasoning behind the voluntary exit programme, Nadella said the initiative was designed to give employees more control over their long-term career and financial prospects.

He also highlighted the importance of ensuring that employees have opportunities to progress within Microsoft, particularly as existing roles and teams undergo changes. Drawing on his own career progression from an individual contributor to CEO, he said employee development and access to new opportunities remained important considerations.

**Microsoft’s Voluntary Exit Offer**

The comments come as [Microsoft rolls out its Voluntary Exit Offer for eligible employees in India](https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/microsoft-offers-voluntary-buyouts-to-60000-employees-as-ai-spending-pressures-costs-ws-l-113436.htm), the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada. The programme has been extended to approximately 60,000 employees across the four countries.

The initiative has raised questions about the company's workforce plans as technology companies navigate changes in job requirements and the increasing role of artificial intelligence.

Acknowledging the scale of the ongoing transition, Nadella said Microsoft could not promise that the workplace would continue to operate as it does today. He stressed the need for the company to communicate openly about the changes and work towards creating new avenues for employee growth.
